lessons.title: The Iterator Protocol ({ value, done })
lessons.description: The iterator protocol defines how to traverse a sequence — return { value, done } from a next() method.

sections.heading: What is an iterator?
paragraphs: An iterator is an object with a next() method that returns { value, done }. It produces values one at a time, tracking its position internally.
list: next() returns { value, done: false } for each item
Returns { done: true } when iteration is complete
The iterator is stateful — it remembers where it left off
Arrays, strings, Maps, Sets all implement the iterator protocol

codeExamples.heading: Manual iterator creation
explanation: The iterator returns { value, done } from each next() call.
The current value is tracked internally (closure).
When done is true, iteration is complete.
You call next() manually — for...of automates this.

practice.task: Create an iterator that produces the letters of a string one at a time. Call next() manually to see each letter.
hints: Store the string and an index in a closure.
Each next() returns the letter at the current index.
When index >= string.length, return { done: true }.

keyTakeaways: An iterator has a next() method returning { value, done }.
done: false means there's more to iterate; done: true means it's finished.
Iterators are stateful — they remember their position.
for...of automates calling next() until done is true.
lessons.challenge: Create an iterator that generates prime numbers up to a given limit.

lessons.title: Custom Iterables using [Symbol.iterator]
lessons.description: Make your objects iterable by implementing the Symbol.iterator method.

sections.heading: The iterable protocol
paragraphs: An iterable is an object that implements [Symbol.iterator], returning an iterator. This lets your objects work with for...of, spread and destructuring.
list: The iterator must have a next() method
The iterable can be used with for...of, [...obj], [a, b] = obj
Built-in iterables: Array, String, Map, Set, TypedArray, NodeList

codeExamples.heading: Making a custom object iterable
explanation: Implement [Symbol.iterator]() to return the iterator (often this).
The next() method produces values one at a time.
for...of calls next() automatically until done is true.
Destructuring also uses the iterator protocol.

practice.task: Create a Queue class that is iterable — for...of should yield elements in FIFO order without removing them.
hints: Each next() returns the element at the current index.

keyTakeaways: Implement [Symbol.iterator] to make any object iterable.
The method returns an iterator with a next() method.
Iterables work with for...of, spread and destructuring.
This protocol is the foundation of JavaScript's iteration system.
lessons.challenge: Create a Tree class that implements depth-first iteration using Symbol.iterator.

lessons.title: Generator Functions (function*) & yield Execution
lessons.description: Generators produce values lazily — pause execution with yield and resume when you need the next value.

sections.heading: What are generators?
paragraphs: Generator functions use function* syntax and the yield keyword to produce values lazily. They pause execution at each yield and resume when the next value is requested.
list: Call the function to get a generator object (doesn't execute yet)
Call .next() to run until the next yield
yield value pauses and produces a value

codeExamples.heading: Generator basics
explanation: Calling the generator function returns a generator object — not the values.
Each .next() runs until the next yield, producing a value.
The function's state (variables, position) is preserved between yields.
Generators are automatically iterable — use with for...of.

practice.task: Write a generator function that yields Fibonacci numbers. Use it with for...of to print the first 10.

keyTakeaways: Generators use function* and yield to produce values lazily.
They pause execution at each yield and resume on the next .next() call.
Generator state is preserved between yields.
Generators are iterable — use with for...of, spread and destructuring.
lessons.challenge: Write a generator that generates all permutations of an array of elements.

lessons.title: Async Generators & for await...of Iteration
lessons.description: Combine async functions with generators to iterate over asynchronous data sources one item at a time.

sections.heading: Async generators
paragraphs: Async generators use async function* and yield Promises. Use for await...of to iterate over them — each value is awaited before processing.
list: async function* name() { } — declares an async generator
yield promise — yields a Promise that is awaited
for await (let value of asyncGen) — iterates asynchronously
Perfect for paginated APIs, streaming data and lazy async operations

codeExamples.heading: Async generator for paginated data
explanation: async function* creates an async generator.
Each yield produces a Promise that for await...of automatically awaits.
The generator pauses until the next page is fetched.
When the generator returns, the loop ends.

practice.task: Write an async generator that yields a countdown from 5 to 1, with a 1-second delay between each number.
hints: Use await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1000)) for delays.

keyTakeaways: Async generators use async function* and yield Promises.
for await...of iterates over async generators, awaiting each value.
Perfect for paginated APIs, streaming data and lazy async operations.
They combine the power of generators and async/await.
lessons.challenge: Build an async generator that reads a file line by line, yielding each line as a string.
